title: El Puesto
label: ch:es-puesto
canDo: I can read a job advert and say what the work asks of me: what it demands, what I am answerable for, what I would be teaching, and when the person I am replacing leaves.

payoff.summary: Read the message or notice this chapter's words exist for, then say the same thing back.
payoff.note: Wordlist derived by the solo-blocker rule (ch440). THE SPINE IS THAT A ROOT YOU OWN PREDICTS HOW A NEW WORD BEHAVES, and two of the five prove it from domains that look unrelated. responsabilidad shares spondere with EL ESPOSO (ch306): a spouse is the one promised, and to be responsable is to be able to promise back. repetir shares petere with EL PEDIDO (ch431, tranche 1), and that one pays MECHANICALLY: pedir goes pido/pides/pide and repetir goes repito/repites/repite, the same e->i break, because they are one Latin verb with and without a prefix -- nobody has to teach the conjugation separately. The repaso states the principle: the return on etymology is not that the stories are charming but that a root you own tells you how an unfamiliar word will behave before anybody explains it. jubilarse closes the debt 435 opened by teaching jubilado without the verb, and iubilare meant TO SHOUT FOR JOY -- the shout came first and the pension after. Also taught: -idad/-bilidad turns an adjective into its quality regularly (dificultad was drafted as an example and REMOVED, being -tad and irregular, so it undercut the rule it illustrated); and -ente/-ante marks the one doing the verb. The payoff separates SE EXIGE (required, without it you are ineligible) from SE VALORARA (merely valued), which is the most useful distinction on a Spanish job advert and is carried entirely by the verb.
